gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many 8-hour workdays a charge lasts on any under-$60 numpad board: the Keychron J5's own figures (3,750 mAh, up to 300 hours) work out to 37.5 workdays and an implied average draw of 12.5 mA, which marks the 300 hours as a low-draw, backlight-off-class figure.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages (techgearden.com, kazsushibistro.com) and two top results (keebkit.com, gearedgaming.com). None of them names the Keychron J5, Gamakay TK101, Attack Shark X98, Womier X98 or Rosewill S96. TechGearDen gives only mAh, with no hours, for the AULA F99 and F75 Pro. Kazsushibistro gives hours only for boards off this question (AOC GK330, a 75% board, 55 h RGB on / 220 h off; anecdotal use on the over-budget AULA F99). KeebKit and Geared Gaming give no battery hours at all. None converts hours to workdays or to an implied draw. The limit on this finding: it is fully sourced for one candidate only (Keychron J5). I could not open a page with the TK101's battery figures, and the Attack Shark store would not load.
decides: As sourced, it confirms the Keychron J5 ($44.99 at keychron.com) as the pick on battery for this question: about 7.5 five-day weeks per charge at the maker's ceiling, though that ceiling implies lighting off. It also takes the Womier X98 out at its maker's store, where it is $84.99; it fits under $60 only at the Best Buy and Newegg listings ChatGPT showed, which I did not open. The Gamakay TK101 ($47.99, 101 keys, 98%) fits the budget and belongs in the table as our linkable row, $3.00 above the J5, but I have no sourced battery hours for it. An unopened lead (search summaries of the PC Gamer review: 4,000 mAh, Gamakay claiming up to 20 hours, the reviewer getting roughly 25-30 hours with RGB at default) would put it at about 2.5 to 3.75 workdays lit. If that is confirmed by opening the review, the TK101 should not be sold on battery and the standout rises to 3.
